gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-inter-tight: Heavy and blunt, Plakkaat bends its letters like single strands of straw, best when big and brief. Inter Tight comes in as a plain sans with rope-like lines and short ascenders, its curve tails held well back.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-karla: Karla has a gaping c and a middle band so tall the lines look stocky and friendly. Karla is the open, approachable half here, while Plakkaat's bent-straw capitals close up nearly to the stem and carry the weight.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-kedebideri: Approachable in the body and heavy in the heading, this pair splits cleanly between closed and open letters. Kedebideri has a skyward x-height and rounded shapes that stay inviting, so it can be sized up a touch without losing its manner, while Plakkaat holds its ground.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-khula: Plakkaat's letters look bent from a single wire, bold and heavy. Khula answers that with a tall, squat-bellied midsection and curves that keep their mouths open, so the pair's strongest quality is a wiry, closed heading set against a body that breathes.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-krub: Chunky bent-straw capitals, closed up nearly to the stem. Krub sits beneath as a sans with a pronounced x-height and pen-lifted curves that leave their loops unfinished, giving the heavy heading some air to push against.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-lexend: Lexend reads big and open, with oversized lowercase and jaws that never clamp shut. Its strongest quality shows against Plakkaat, whose bold bent-straw letters curl nearly closed, so one side stays tight while the other lets every curve breathe.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-lexend-deca: Plakkaat brings heavy, bent-straw capitals whose terminals sweep nearly back to the stem, so it earns its place at a large size. And Lexend Deca stays plain and unshaded below, with small-looking capitals and terminals that stop short of curling in.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-liter: Liter is a plain sans with no stroke contrast at all, and its lowercase stands tall. Liter keeps wide mouths on its round forms, which settles the eye after Plakkaat's heavy, nearly closed bent-straw shapes.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-mada: Plakkaat's line holds one width on every letter, bold and heavy. Mada runs a towering midzone with curves that refuse to close, so a long page of it feels open and approachable beneath that dense, closed heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans lifts a high mean line across every word and gives each curve a generous opening. Plakkaat is best at heavy, thread-like single strokes, while Martel Sans does its best work in open, modern text.
